Domain: identify an image format from its own bytes
Where we actually are — memory was stale
Before authoring anything I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt: 355 file records, 353 SHA-256 matches, the two exceptions being export.sh (excluded by design) and LICENSE (elided since Slice 46). Zero unexplained mismatches.

The important finding is that my memory of this project was several slices behind the tree. It said Slice 47 was next up and predicted 1166 tests. The tree says otherwise:

docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md ends at M6 Slice 50 — "the last surface that read the menu flat, and the rule that had nowhere to be tested."
claude-terminal.txt reports total: 1202, failed: 0 and 17/17 end-to-end scenarios passing three times over, with every local CI gate green.
Slices 47 (section resequence), 48 (item resequence), 49 (guest-visible section description), and 50 (MenuGrouping + the kitchen 86 panel) have all landed. Stage 3 and Stages 3a–3c of MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md are closed. Spec is at v1.35, §16.4 census at 25.
So there was nothing to resume. I re-planned from the tree's own "what is still open" list, which says plainly: "Ordering is complete for both tables, every menu surface groups by heading… The next stage is Stage 4." Stage 4 is images.

The slice I started building — Slice 51, Stage 4a
Cut at the schema and data access, exactly where Stage 2 was cut, and for the identical reason: two new tables that touch nothing existing are green by construction rather than by inspection. Stage 4's four surface consequences (the route, the CSP question, the no-resizing ruling, the 375px layout) stay in 4b — and one of them is a genuine unresolved design question, since these admin pages are static SSR and a file upload there is not the InputFile shape.

Two files are written and complete:

src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Migrations/0006_menu_item_images.sql — menu_item_image (one image per item via UNIQUE on the referencing column, which is also the index) and menu_item_image_event (attached | replaced | removed, two paired biconditionals).

src/MyRestaurant.Domain/Menu/ImageFormat.cs — a pure signature check (PNG/JPEG/WebP), in Domain on F-100's argument, so the interesting cases don't cost a container.

Three rulings came out of designing it, and they are the reason I think this cut is right:

No byte_length column. octet_length(bytes) is the length. A stored integer beside it is one fact written twice — F-65's mechanism, in a place where a single UPDATE can make the copies disagree. It is a column on the event table, because a removal deletes the bytes and that is then the only place the number can live.
No pixel_width/pixel_height. Nothing in this stack can measure them, so they would be the client's unverifiable claim stored in the indicative.
The 512 KiB cap is stated once, in the DDL. The write reports a refusal by reading the constraint name off the PostgreSQL error rather than restating the number — which is why there are two constraints instead of one BETWEEN, so an empty file and an oversized photo get different sentences.
Those three are F-101: the plan's own DDL sketch carried all three columns, and a design document's SQL is gated by nothing, so a duplicated fact survives into the migration that creates it — and a migration is the one artefact this project never edits.

What remains, and what I need from you
I hit the tool ceiling partway through. Still to author: the Dapper store, the two test classes (7 unit + 11 integration facts), ADR-0015, the DI registration, SchemaMigrationRunnerTests' two relation rows, and the full documentation set — spec v1.36 (§7, §8.1, §8.2, §16.4, Appendix A, changelog), the plan, BUILD_PROGRESS.md, DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, _CHANGES.md, and the census floor 25 → 27.

Predicted count: 1202 → 1222 (18 new assertions plus 2 theory rows). No files to delete.

Say continue and I'll finish it and package the archive. Two things worth your veto first, though, since they're cheaper to reverse now than after extraction:

Stage 4a re-opens an obligation you just closed. A DataAccess pair with no surface is precedented — IMenuSectionAdministration sat there for seven slices — but it is the obligation Slice 43 discharged, and I'd be recording it as deliberately re-opened. If you'd rather not, the alternative slice is the §16.3 scenario for the two resequencing verbs, which the plan names as the largest end-to-end gap in the menu.
ImageFormat lives in Domain, which adds a second test class and moves the census two rather than one. Collapsing it into the DataAccess write would cost one class but put the truncated-signature and not-a-WebP-RIFF cases behind a container.
Claude reached its tool-use limit for this turn.

src/MyRestaurant.Domain/Menu/ is a new directory — Domain has never had one. git status should show seven modifications and six untracked paths. Migrations/*.sql is globbed as an EmbeddedResource, so 0006 needs no .csproj edit — but it does need git add, or it is invisible to every gate.

Modified (seven, all complete)
OrdersServiceCollectionExtensions.cs · SchemaMigrationRunnerTests.cs · TestingSectionContractTests.cs · TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (v1.36) · MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md · DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md · BUILD_PROGRESS.md

The finding: F-101
The plan's Stage 4 DDL sketch had byte_length (which is octet_length(bytes) — F-65's mechanism, seventh occurrence) plus pixel_width and pixel_height, which are worse: the same stage's own prose says nothing in this stack can open an image, so both could only ever have been the browser's word recorded in the indicative. The mechanism is the finding — three gates read that document and none reads a fenced SQL block for meaning, so a sketch is unchecked prose with a schema's authority, and its destination is the one artefact this project never edits. All three dropped before 0006 was written. No gate added, on F-41.

Menu progress
0006 adds two tables and touches nothing existing — 0003's cut again, green by construction. OrderTestWorld needed no edit. ADR-0015 rules bytea on F-38's argument, and the reversibility direction is what decides it. The cap is written once, in the DDL, reported by constraint name. ImageFormat checks the declared type against the bytes' signature — both halves of WebP's RIFF header — in Domain on F-100's argument.

No OPERATIONS.md edit, which is the storage decision paying out on arrival: the recovery set is still two artefacts.

Predicted test count: 1202 → 1223
Where	Assertions
ImageFormatTests	8
MenuItemImageTests	11
SchemaMigrationRunnerTests theory rows	2
§16.4 census and floor move 25 → 27. §16.3 stays at seventeen.

Worth knowing: the gate simulation caught a real error before packaging. §16.4 said seven assertions for ImageFormatTests where the file holds eight — F-70's shape, in the section written to stop it. Both the paragraph and the arithmetic now say eight. That is why 1223 and not 1222.

Two things flagged for your veto
This re-opens the obligation Slice 43 closed — two data-access services with no caller outside their tests. It's the weaker form (nothing behind IMenuWorkflow), and it's named in §7, the DI comment, the plan and the build log. To reverse: hold all of 0006 until 4b.
ImageFormat in Domain moves the census two rather than one. To reverse: fold it into the write as a private static, delete ImageFormatTests, drop the floor to 26 — at the cost of putting the malformed-signature cases behind a container.
Not verified
Nothing compiled, no database, no browser. The four likeliest reds, in order: no bytea round trip was performed; whether PostgresException.ConstraintName is populated for a check violation (the cap outcome depends on it, and any other check violation is rethrown by design, so a miss shows up as a throw in one named fact); whether regexp_match(pg_get_constraintdef(…)) finds the cap; and whether the ReadOnlySpan<byte> collection expressions compile — a shape this tree hasn't used before.

Run bash run.sh --smoke as well as ci_local.sh — without a container engine the integration facts skip, which would leave 0006 unexercised.
